title: Ratio, Proportion & Partnership
intro: A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind; a proportion says two ratios are equal. The single most useful idea is the common multiplier: if a:b = 3:4, write the quantities as 3x and 4x, and one equation fixes x. Partnership is just ratio applied to money and time — profit divides in the ratio of (capital x months). This chapter builds the multiplier habit that also powers mixtures, ages and partnership.

topics.name: Ratio Basics
topics.details: Express a ratio in lowest terms by dividing by the HCF. To compare ratios, cross-multiply or convert to decimals. To combine a:b and b:c into a:b:c, scale so the common term b matches (take its LCM). The multiplier method — letting the parts be 2x, 3x, 5x — turns almost every ratio word problem into one linear equation.

solved.problem: If a:b = 2:3 and b:c = 4:5, find a:b:c.
solved.solution: Make b common (LCM 12): a:b = 8:12, b:c = 12:15. So a:b:c = 8:12:15.

solved.problem: Two numbers are in ratio 5:7 and their sum is 96. Find them.

unsolved.problem: Two numbers ratio 7:9, difference 30. Find them.

topics.name: Proportion & Variation
topics.details: In a proportion a:b = c:d, the product of the means equals the product of the extremes (b x c = a x d). Direct variation means y = kx (both rise together); inverse variation means xy = k (one rises as the other falls). The mean proportional between a and b is root(ab); the third proportional to a and b is b^2/a.

solved.problem: If 12 men finish a job in 8 days, how many days for 16 men (inverse)?
solved.solution: Men x days constant: 12 x 8 = 96 = 16 x d -> d = 6 days.

unsolved.problem: y varies directly as x; y = 12 when x = 4. y at x = 7?

topics.name: Dividing in a Ratio
topics.details: Many SSC sums add or change one part of a ratio. Convert the ratio to actual parts with a multiplier, apply the change, and re-read the new ratio. When a quantity is added equally to all parts, the ratio changes; when one part is changed, set up the new equality. Coins/notes problems (a:b:c counts with different denominations) are ratio plus weighting.

solved.problem: A sum of 1100 is divided among A, B, C as 2:3:6. Find C share.
Two numbers 3:5; if 8 is added to each they become 2:3. Find them.
A bag has 1-rupee, 2-rupee and 5-rupee coins in the ratio 3:2:1, with a total value of 96 rupees. Find the number of 2-rupee coins.
solved.solution: Counts 3x, 2x, x. Value = 3x(1) + 2x(2) + x(5) = 3x + 4x + 5x = 12x = 96 -> x = 8. So 2-rupee coins = 2x = 16.

solved.problem: Incomes are in ratio 5:4 and expenditures in ratio 3:2. If each saves 6000, find the incomes.
solved.solution: Incomes 5k, 4k; expenditures 3m, 2m. 5k - 3m = 6000 and 4k - 2m = 6000. From the second, 2k - m = 3000 -> m = 2k - 3000. Substitute: 5k - 3(2k - 3000) = 6000 -> 5k - 6k + 9000 = 6000 -> k = 3000. Incomes = 15000 and 12000.

unsolved.problem: Divide 6300 among A,B,C as 1:3:5. B share?
Ratio 2:3; add 5 to each -> 3:4. Find numbers.
Ratio 5:7; subtract 4 from each -> 1:2. Find them.

topics.name: Partnership & Profit Sharing
topics.details: In a partnership, profit divides in the ratio of each partner's contribution to the business = capital x time invested. If everyone invests for the same period, profit divides simply in the ratio of capitals. A working partner may take an extra salary or commission off the top before the remaining profit is shared. Always reduce each partner to a single capital-months figure first.

solved.problem: A invests 5000 for 12 months, B invests 6000 for 8 months. A profit of 1800 is earned — find each share.
A and B invest 8000 and 12000 for the same time. Divide a profit of 5000.
A starts with 30000; after 4 months B joins with 45000. Year-end profit ratio?
Three partners invest in ratio 3:4:5 for equal time. Profit 24000 — largest share?

unsolved.problem: Ratio of capitals 2:3:5, same time, profit 30000. Smallest share?
A invests for 12m, B (same amount) for 8m. Ratio?

shortcuts: Always introduce a common multiplier x and form one equation.
Combine a:b and b:c by scaling b to its LCM.
Partnership: reduce each partner to capital x months, then share in that ratio.
Same time invested -> profit splits in the ratio of capitals.
mistakes: Adding ratio terms without multiplying by x first.
Forgetting to scale the common term when chaining a:b and b:c.
Using capital only (ignoring time) in partnership profit sharing.
Treating a:b = c:d as a + d = b + c instead of a x d = b x c.
pyq: SSC favours add-to-each ratio sums and capital x time partnership. Coins-in-a-bag and income-expenditure-savings problems recur in Tier 2.

flashcards.a: a x d = b x c

summary: Use a common multiplier for every ratio sum, equate cross-products for proportion, and remember mean proportional = root(ab). Partnership profit splits as capital x time. These habits also drive mixtures, ages and DI.
